(GIRISH CHATNI)
XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT

The P.I., of Mahadevapura Police Station, Bengaluru, has filed the present charge sheet against the accused No.1 to 3 for the offence punishable under sections 447, 427, 420, 354, 506 R/w Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code.
2. BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :

It is the case of the complainant that, accused No.1 sold the property site No.4,
comprised in Sy.No.24/3 situated at B.Narayanapura, Krishnarajapura Hobli,
Bengaluru South Taluk, measuring West 27 feet and South 60 feet, in total 1620 Sq.Feet to the complainant by name Smt.Shanthi Abraham for an amount of Rs.8,90,000/- and executed Sale deed and registered the same in K.R.Pura Sub-Registrar Office on 08.04.2005 in favour of complainant.

It is further alleged that, with an intention to cheat the complainant, on 06.04.1990 the accused persons have made amended Will and the accused No.2, who is the brother of accused No.1 Mrs Shanthi Abraham vs C.Nagaraja on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30143168/
2 executed Gift Deed in favour of his son by name K.Lakshmipathi i.e., accused No.3 on 13.04.2017 and registered the same in K.R.Pura Sub- Registrar Office and cheated the complainant.
It is further alleged that, CW.1 and 2 with an intention to build a house placed house materials in the said site and the work was completed up to laying of foundation of house.

It is further alleged that, when CW.1 and 2 went to Kerala State due to some work, by that time accused No.3 went to the said site and sold the materials i.e., stones, Jellies,
Bricks and Dust materials and caused loss of Rs.5,00,000/- to CW.1 and 2.

It is further alleged that,
on 13.07.2017 at 7.00 AM, when CW.1 to 4 went to the said site, by that time accused No.1 to 3 illegally made tresspass in the site and picked up quarrel with CW.1 to 4 by threatening that the said site belongs to them and accused No.3 outraged the modesty of CW.1 by pulling her hand.

Based on the typed complain lodged by the complainant, CW.7 registered the case against the accused No.1 to 3 in PS.Crime No.355/2017 for the offence punishable U/s 420, 447, 468, 471, 420, 354, 506 R/w 34 of IPC and forwarded FIR to the court.
Investigating officers/CW.7 and 8 investigated the matter.

CW.8 after completion of the investigation has submitted final report against the accused No.1 to 3 alleging the commission of offence punishable U/s 447, 427, 420, 354, 506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC.
3.
Upon receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the above said offences alleged against the accused No.1 to 3 and registered the criminal case against them.
4. After registering the case, the accused No.1 has appeared before the court and was enlarged on bail.
The accused No.2 was reported to be dead.
During the course of the trial accused No.3 reported to be dead.
Copy of the charge sheet and its' enclosures were furnished to the accused No.1 in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Sufficient grounds were made out to frame charges.

Hence,
charges framed and read over to the accused No.1.
He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

5. In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined 03 witnesses out of 08 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 to P.W.8 and got marked 30 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.30 and closed its side.
Thereafter, the accused No.1 was examined as provided U/s 313 of Cr.P.C by explaining incriminating evidence appearing against him.
The accused No.1 has denied the same and has not produced any oral or documentary evidence.
6. Heard both sides.
Perused the materials on record.

2.
7. The points that arise for my consideration are;
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 06.04.1990 the with a common intention made amended Will and the accused No.2, who is the brother of accused No.1 executed Gift Deed in favour of his son by name K.Lakshmipathi i.e., accused No.3 on 13.04.2017 and registered the site No.4 in K.R.Pura Sub-Registrar Office and cheated the complainant and Mrs Shanthi Abraham vs C.Nagaraja on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30143168/
3 thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.420 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

sentences.text:
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 13.07.2017 at 7.00 AM,
accused No.1 along with accused No.2 & 3 with a common intention illegally entered into the site No.4, Sy.No.24/3, B.Narayanapura, Krishnarajapura Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk of complainant and made criminal trespass and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.447 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, accused No.1 along with accused No.2 & 3 in furtherance of common intention, accused No.3 went to the said site and sold the materials i.e., stone, Jelli, Bricks and Dust and caused loss of Rs.5,00,000/- to CW.1 and 2 and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.427 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?
4.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the above mentioned date,
time and place, accused No.1 along with accused No.2 & 3 in furtherance of common intention threatened CW.1 to 4 with dire consequences and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

5. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the above mentioned date,
time and place, accused No.1 along with accused No.2 & 3 in furtherance of common intention,
among them accused No.3 outraged the modesty of CW.1 by pulling her hand and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.354 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?
6. What Order?

8. My findings on the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 to 5 : In the Negative.
 Point No.6 : As per the final order  for the following;
 REASONS  9. POINT Nos.1 to 5:-
As these Five points are interlinked, I have taken up these points together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts & evidence.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1, the prosecution has to establish that, the accused No.1 along with other accused persons with an intention to cheat the com- plainant first sold the site No.4 to the complainant, thereafter, by making amendment to the Will, accused No.2 made gift of the said site to the accused No.3,
accused persons have made tresspass, accused No.3 by selling the building materials Mrs Shanthi Abraham vs C.Nagaraja on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30143168/
4 caused loss of Rs.5,00,000/- to CW.1, accused No.3 outraged the modesty of CW.1 by holding her hand and dragged and also threatened CW.1 to 4 with dire consequences.
10. On perusal of the entire materials on record, the prosecution has failed to secure the presence of CW.1 to 5 and led their evidence.
CW.1 to 5 are material and vital witnesses.
11. The prosecution has examined an independent wit- ness CW.6 as PW.1, wherein, he has not supported the case of the prosecution.

The learned APP appearing for the state has treated the witness as hostile and fully cross examined him, wherein,
nothing was elicited from his mouth in order to prove with regard to the amendment made to the Will.

12. The prosecution examined the investigating offi- cers CW.7 and 8, wherein, they have deposed with regard to the investigation being carried out by them in pursuance of the complaint filed by the complainant.
The said witnesses have deposed regarding the filing of complaint, registering till com- pletion of investigation.

13. As already discussed in my earlier paragraph of discussions, the person, who got cheated and the victim i.e., CW.1 to 4 have not been examined by the prosecution and have failed to secure their presence before the court.
Mere on the evidence of investigating officers, it is not safe to come to the conclusion that, the accused No.1 has committed the of- fence as alleged by the complainant.

14. On over all perusal of the materials on record, the evidence on record both by way of oral and documentary evi- dence are not helpful and sufficient to the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond all reasonable doubt.
In such circumstances, the benefit of doubt has to be extended to accused No.1 and he is entitled for acquittal.
Accordingly, the Point Nos.1 to 5 are answered in the "Negative".

15. Point No.6:- In view of the findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 is acquitted of the offence punishable under sections 447, 427, 420, 354, 506 R/w Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code.
The personal bond and surety bond of the accused No.1 shall be in force for the period of 6 months and thereafter it shall be cancelled without further orders.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and typed by her, corrected by me and then signed and pronounced in the Open Court on this date the 12th Day of March, 2025.)
(GIRISH CHATNI) XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU ANNEXURE 1.
